info.title: ERP Pilot — v1 API
info.summary: Reads across the modules, drafts into the ledger, nothing that posts
info.description:
Authentication is a Sanctum bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer erp_…`), obtained from
`POST /api/v1/auth/token` with credentials or from **Settings → API Tokens** in the app.

Three rules explain almost every design decision below.

**Abilities narrow, roles authorise.** A token can only ever reach what its owning user
could reach, and only the subset its abilities name. A stolen accountant's token mints no
invoices; a Super Admin's token with `sales:read` posts no journals.

**Money is a string.** Amounts arrive as two-decimal strings — `decimal:2` is the cast on
every model column in this application. Parse them with a decimal type, not a float.

**Reads are free, writes are drafts.** The only mutating endpoint in v1 creates an
unposted draft journal, validated by the same form request the screen uses. Posting a
journal, voiding one, and touching the ledger require a person.

Pagination, search and filtering use the same query vocabulary as the tables in the
application itself — `search`, `sort`, `dir`, `page`, `per_page`, `filters[...]` — so one
behaviour cannot drift between what an integrator sees and what an accountant sees.

parameters.name: approved_only
parameters.description: Approved and locked budgets only — excludes drafts.

get.description: Plan headers with line counts. The amounts live on the variance report, not here.

get.summary: Budget versus actual for one budget

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: YYYY-MM. Omit to aggregate every month the budget carries lines for.

get.description: Actuals are read from the posted ledger at request time and never cached, so this cannot drift from the trial balance. `favourable` is nature-dependent — do not derive it from the sign of `variance`.

post.description: Validated by the same form request the screen uses — same rules, same balance tolerance, same 422 messages — and always created as a draft. Posting is not available over v1 by design: an integration bug then leaves an unposted draft instead of a ledger that needs correcting. Domain refusals (an open fiscal year covering the date, a posting account) also answer 422 with the screen's sentence, never a 500.

get.summary: Read one journal and its lines
get.description: Debits and credits per line, as decimal strings, with the posting account resolved to code and name.

get.summary: Trial balance as at a date
get.description: The identical rows and sign convention as the on-screen report: a `debit`-nature account reports debit − credit, everything else reports credit − debit. Read `balance` with `balance_side`; a client that assumes credit-positive will read every asset account backwards and still get plausible numbers.

get.summary: Who am I, and what may this token do
get.description: The owning user's effective permissions alongside this token's abilities. This is the answer to "my token works but returns 403": the token is almost always narrower than the user.

post.description: The secret is returned once — only its sha256 hash is stored, so it can never be read back. `abilities` narrows what this token may reach and can never widen what the owning user's roles allow. Bad credentials answer 401 with the same message whether the address is unknown or the password is wrong.

delete.summary: Revoke the token making the call
delete.description: A browser session has no token to revoke and gets 400 rather than a silent success. Revoking the token you are authenticated with ends the request's own authority — that is intended, not a bug.

get.description: Generated from the live route table on every request, so it can only describe what this deployment actually serves. `docs/openapi.json` is the same bytes, committed for review; `php artisan api:spec --check` fails when they part company.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Invoice number, invoice date or created_at — the columns the on-screen table searches.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Default 25, capped at 100. Want more? Paginate.

get.description: One page of invoices. Money is exact two-decimal strings, so `total_amount` can be added up without floating-point drift.

get.summary: Read one invoice, by id or invoice number

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Numeric invoice id or the human invoice number, which is what a customer quotes back at you.

get.description: Includes the VAT-bearing lines. A row you may not see answers 404 rather than 403 — that the document exists is not information for outside the ACL.

bearerAuth.description: A Sanctum personal access token. Opaque by design: it is a random secret and a lookup, not a self-describing credential, so revoking it is immediate.

MoneyString.description: An exact amount as a two-decimal string, never a float. Every model here casts decimals `decimal:2`, and JSON floats are how an integration ends up one paisa short and blaming the ledger.

PageMeta.description: The same pagination envelope the on-screen tables consume.

journal_id.description: The posted journal, when there is one — the join back to the ledger.

nature.description: Which side the account normally carries.

balance_side.description: Read `balance` together with this: the sign is per-account, not globally credit-positive.

favourable.description: Nature-dependent: a debit account is on-plan when actual ≤ budget, a credit account when actual ≥ budget. Do not infer this from the sign of `variance`.

lines.description: Must balance to the paisa — the check runs through `JournalBalance`, the same object the screen and `post()` use, so a journal accepted here is never rejected later for a reason the API did not state.

account_id.description: Must be a posting account: a group header is refused.

token.description: Format `id|secret`, prefixed `erp_` so a leak is recognisable. Returned once.

permissions.description: What the owning user may do. A token may do less than this, never more.

401.description: No token, a revoked one, or an expired one. A request without `Accept: application/json` still gets this JSON body, never a redirect to the login form.

403.description: The owning user lacks the permission, or this token lacks the ability. `X-request-id` is not returned; the message names which of the two it was.

404.description: No row matches, including for a row you may not see — reading 404 for someone else's document is itself a leak.

422.description: Validation failed. Field keys match the request body exactly, so a client can map them back.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded: 60 requests/minute per user across all their tokens, 5/minute for the token exchange.
